coordinates.note: Located in Braavos — same schematic position as city

founding.description: Founded from wealth hidden by the city's founders in an abandoned iron mine — hence 'Iron Bank'.

history.event: Iron Bank originates from wealth cached in an abandoned iron mine by Braavos's escaped-slave founders.

At the Uncloaking of Uthero, the Iron Bank pays generous settlements to descendants of masters whose ships the founders took — but refuses to pay for the value of the slaves, establishing its anti-slavery stance.
The Iron Bank withdraws support from the Lannister-controlled Iron Throne and begins financing Stannis Baratheon. Tycho Nestoris leads the delegation to Stannis at Castle Black.

metadata.description: One of the most powerful financial institutions in the known world. When kings or nations default on debts, the Iron Bank funds their rivals. 'The Iron Bank will have its due' is its guiding motto.
metadata.role_in_sealord_election: The keyholders of the Iron Bank participate in the election of the Sealord of Braavos.
metadata.narratorText: The Iron Bank of Braavos does not forgive. When the Iron Throne stopped paying its debts, the bank turned to Stannis Baratheon. Princes have learned — it is easier to move the stones of the Titan than to escape what you owe the Iron Bank.

coordinates.note: House of Black and White — Braavos harbor island

founding.period: Valyrian era, among slaves in the mines
founding.description: The Faceless Men originated among the slaves in the mines of Valyria. Some traditions hold that the first Faceless Man was a slave who prayed to all the gods of his fellow slaves simultaneously and heard them answer as one — the Many-Faced God, the God of Death.

history.event: The Faceless Men are said to have played a role in liberating slaves who founded Braavos, intertwined with the city's founding.
Ser Jorah Mormont reports on the activities of the Faceless Men for Lord Varys; Arya Stark later arrives in Braavos and trains at the House of Black and White.

metadata.description: A guild of assassins based in the House of Black and White in Braavos. They worship the Many-Faced God (the God of Death) and are famous for their ability to change their appearance using the faces of the dead. Their services are extraordinarily expensive and often exacted in non-monetary forms.
metadata.temple: House of Black and White, Braavos
metadata.narratorText: A man says: Valar Morghulis. A woman says: Valar Dohaeris. All men must serve. The Faceless Men take no payment in gold alone. A face for a face. A life for a life. They are death wearing many faces.

coordinates.note: Palace of the Sealord, Braavos — schematic

history.event: Sealord Uthero Zalyne performs the Uncloaking of Uthero, revealing Braavos to the world during its 111th founding festival.

metadata.description: The ruler of Braavos, elected for life by the city's wealthy elite and the keyholders of the Iron Bank. Not a hereditary position. The Sealord commands Braavos's formidable fleet and represents the city in diplomacy.
metadata.election_method: Elected for life by wealthy elite and Iron Bank keyholders — not hereditary
metadata.narratorText: The Sealord of Braavos rules from his palace, surrounded by exotic creatures and advisors. He is elected for life by those with wealth and influence — and the Iron Bank holds more influence than any. When a Sealord dies, the city holds its breath until a new one is named.

history.event: The Triarch system established as Volantis's governing structure, requiring three Triarchs elected annually. Only those with Valyrian blood — the old families — may vote or stand for election.
Tiger faction Triarchs drive the Century of Blood expansionist wars following the Doom of Valyria.
Elephant faction Triarchs take control following Volantis's defeat in the Century of Blood; Elephant dominance lasts ~300 years.

metadata.description: Three Triarchs govern Volantis, elected annually. Two factions contest the election: the Tigers (old military aristocracy, pro-expansion, pro-Valyrian legacy) and the Elephants (merchants, pro-trade, pro-peace). Only those of Valyrian blood may vote or stand. The Elephants have dominated for three centuries at the time of the main series.
metadata.voter_requirement: Must be of Valyrian blood (old families only)
metadata.narratorText: Three Triarchs. Three votes. One city divided between the memory of empire and the pragmatism of trade. The Elephants have won for three hundred years — but the Tigers have not forgotten what Volantis once was.

history.event: The Bearded Priests establish religious dominance over Norvos, becoming the city's true rulers and selecting its council of magisters.

metadata.description: The theocratic rulers of Norvos. The Bearded Priests worship a deity whose name is kept secret from outsiders, known only to initiates. They select the council of magisters that nominally governs the city, but real power rests with the priests. They maintain a holy guard of slave soldiers branded with an axe. Life in Norvos is governed by the three great bells: Noom, Narrah, and Nyel.
metadata.deity: Secret — name known only to initiates
metadata.holy_guard: Slave soldiers branded with an axe
metadata.narratorText: The Bearded Priests of Norvos keep their god's name as closely as they keep their hearts — a secret within a secret. They ring the three bells that command the life of every citizen. They choose who rules. They are the law, the faith, and the sword of Norvos.

coordinates.note: Temple of the Black Goat, Qohor — schematic

history.event: The worship of the Black Goat of Qohor is established in the city, demanding daily blood sacrifices.
During the Battle of Qohor, Qohorik nobles offer their own children to the Black Goat in desperation as the Dothraki approach. The Unsullied hold the gates.

metadata.description: The patron deity of Qohor, worshipped through daily blood sacrifices. In times of crisis, the faithful have offered their own children. The Black Goat cult is intertwined with the city's merchant oligarchy and its dark reputation for sorcerous craftsmanship.
metadata.sacrifice: Daily blood sacrifice required; in extreme crisis, noble children have been offered
metadata.narratorText: Each dawn in Qohor, blood is spilled for the Black Goat. It has always been so. When Khal Temmo's fifty thousand rode toward the walls, nobles carried their own children to the altars. The god is satisfied, or the god is not — the city breathes either way.

history.event: Following the Doom of Valyria, the Pentoshi magisters establish a system where they hold real power while electing a Prince as a ceremonial figurehead. The Prince may be sacrificed (executed) if the city fails in war or suffers famine.

metadata.description: The true rulers of Pentos, drawn from the Great Families. They elect the Prince of Pentos as a figurehead. The Prince cannot act on trade, justice, or war without their approval, and risks execution if the city suffers major failures.
metadata.prince_status: Figurehead — elected by magisters; can be executed if city fails
metadata.narratorText: The magisters of Pentos hold the true reins of the city. The Prince sits on his throne and signs what they place before him. If he protests, they remind him of the tradition: a Prince who fails the city is given to the gods.
